subject: Benchmark spec & action commitments (latency/throughput targets)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Tim Carter <tim.carter@novaretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + initial targets for Nova Retail benchmark

Tim — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have an agreed starting point for the benchmark run. This is focused on the storefront personalization flows you mentioned (short completions + streaming product summaries).

Key target commitments (we proposed; please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for non-streaming (up to 128 tokens).
- Streaming: time-to-first-token p95 <= 220ms; chunk tail-latency p95 <= 450ms for 4-token chunks.
- Throughput: steady-state 110 req/s sustained for 30m with median tokens per request ~60.
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent sessions with per-session KV cache preserved for streaming.
- Quality: same prompt set ROUGE/semantic pass-rate target >= 92% vs your golden set (we'll rely on your scoring harness).

Asks from Nova Retail:
1) Share the representative prompt/response bundle (we agreed on an anonymized sample) — you mentioned ~300 prompts across three personas.
2) Clarify any PII handling requirements for prompts we should avoid caching.
3) Confirm calendar window for a run (we suggested Mon/Tue next week).

Attachments referenced: prompt bundle (please upload to the shared Drive link), and we'll send a benchmark instructions doc + measurement matrix from our side.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: upload anonymized prompt bundle and note any PII rows (Tim).
- Us: share benchmark instructions + measurement matrix and a short run script for reproducibility (Ben).
- Align on run window and an internal war room (Ben + Laura + Marissa + Nova ops).

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

From: Tim Carter <tim.carter@novaretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@novaretail.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 12:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + initial targets for Nova Retail benchmark

Ben — thanks, this looks good. A few clarifying points before we lock targets and upload artifacts.

1) Latency:
- The 200ms p95 non-stream target is aggressive but acceptable for our core short-completion workflow (catalog lookup + 1-2 sentence personalization). We do expect a small portion of requests with longer context (up to 256 tokens) — can you confirm a graceful fallback profile if those exceed the 200ms SLO?

2) Streaming:
- Time-to-first-token target is important. For streaming we care about both inter-chunk jitter and first-byte. Our business requirement: first-byte within 300ms for 95% and inter-chunk jitter p95 < 200ms. You proposed 220ms first-byte — fine if inter-chunk jitter is inside 200ms.

3) Throughput & Concurrency:
- We'll provide a traffic mix file (spike + steady). Do you support load shaping so we can reproduce a spike scenario? We also need isolation for this run (so customer traffic doesn't hit the cluster).

4) Data handling:
- We'll redact PII but will flag ~12 prompts that reference internal IDs — those should not be cached; please confirm the instruction is respected in your harness.

Schedule: Monday (May 3) morning PT looks best for us. Procurement looped in for the NDA/access checklist (procurement@novaretail.com).

Thanks — Tim

Tim — great questions, summary inline below and a tightened set of commitments.

- Fallback for longer contexts: We'll route requests >128 tokens to a warmed 'long-context' variant; performance target for that path is p95 <= 420ms. We will include that explicitly in the measurement matrix.
- Streaming jitter: we will target first-byte p95 <= 220ms and inter-chunk jitter p95 <= 180ms; we will record jitter distribution per-session in the run artifacts.
- Load shaping: yes, we will run with a dedicated test window using our Dedicated pool (isolated) and apply the spike profile you provide. We'll publish the exact load script so you can reproduce the shape locally if needed.
- PII: acknowledged — please mark the rows; our harness will set a per-prompt cache-disable flag.

Proposed mutual action plan (owners & dates):
1) Thu Apr 29 — Nova: upload anonymized prompt bundle + spike/steady traffic profiles (Tim).
2) Fri Apr 30 — Redwood: send benchmark_instructions_v1.md and measurement_matrix_v1.xlsx + run script (Ben + Laura).
3) Mon May 3 09:00 PT — bench run window start; Redwood provides run engineer on call (Marissa).
4) Tue May 4 — shared artifact handoff and readout (Ben + Nova ops).

If that looks right I'll have Laura attach the instructions and matrix today. Ben

--
Ben Carter

- measurement_matrix_v1.xlsx: defines every metric we will capture (p50/p95/p99 latency, first-byte, inter-chunk-intervals, jitter, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/s, errors), the sampling cadence, and the artifact format (CSV + JSON summary).
- novaretail_prompt_bundle_v1.json: stub included in Drive; please confirm the redaction column is complete.

Attachment stubs: (we did not embed raw binaries in email)
- Attachment: benchmark_instructions_v1.md (text)
- Attachment: measurement_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

- We'll run three distinct scenarios (steady, single spike x10, and mixed bursts) and preserve raw logs per scenario.
- The run script will compute per-prompt quality deltas and include a reproducibility manifest (seed, model hash, kernel selection snapshot).
